_doc: Performance budgets for the perf-guardrails skill. Consumed by
tests/e2e/test_perf_budgets.py (measurement + gating) and scripts/perf_triage.py
(priority checklist). Two levels per metric, per spec D2 (.agents/specs/playwright-e2e.md):
budget  — advisory. A breach is reported in .agents/reports/perf/last-run.json and
raises the route's priority in the triage checklist. It never fails a test.
ceiling — blocking. Generous enough that only a real regression (an N+1 explosion,
a hung query, a render stall) trips it; a breach fails the perf test.
Units: *_ms are milliseconds; queries is DB statements per request (deterministic, so
its ceiling can be tight). backend_ms is measured SERVER-SIDE (request_started ->
request_finished inside the app process), not client wall-clock. lcp_ms is Chromium's
largest-contentful-paint on a warm cache, median of 3 — a local regression tripwire,
NOT a real-user metric; production LCP truth is the Faro RUM web-vitals stream.
Calibrated 2026-07-18 from a real run on an empty-org baseline (last-run.json):
API medians 3.6-34ms, page shells ~4ms, LCP 56-108ms, queries 2-11. Budgets sit at
roughly 4x the worst observed value; ceilings where only a real regression lands.
The /api/core/dashboard/summary override was a 38-query ratchet until 2026-08-29,
when the endpoint moved its DAG-heavy slice to the shared system-findings cache (its
own _why has the detail). Recalibrate with the procedure in the SKILL.md rather than
hand-tuning numbers to make a red run green.
measure.api entries are normally a bare route string (GET, no body). A route that
requires a request body to be measured meaningfully (e.g. a POST-only solve/compute
endpoint) uses the object form {route, method, body} instead — test_perf_budgets.py
sends `body` as the JSON payload with CSRF headers attached, same as any other
mutating core-API call in the E2E suite.

_why: Added 2026-08-27 by a perf-guardrails review of MR !181 (Core tab 15.8s -> 2.7s).
This is the Core page's hottest endpoint -- it runs the whole system-check suite,
including a DAG traversal per expired-with-stock raw material -- and it had no
budget at all while three separate widgets called it on every page load.
Calibrated per SKILL.md from three runs on the E2E fixture org: queries 11/11/11,
backend_ms medians 12.7/15.2/13.2. queries is PINNED at the observed 11 as a
ratchet (must only ever go down); backend_ms budget is ~4x the worst median.
CAVEAT, deliberately written down rather than assumed away: this fixture org has
ONE expired-with-stock raw material. A probe against the same code measured +2
queries per additional expired raw material (1 -> 9 queries, 10 -> 27), so on a
real org (whistlebird_test: ~47) this endpoint issues ~100 queries per request
and a fixture-calibrated ceiling will never see it. Fixing that means one
multi-root traverse() instead of one per root -- see the review notes.
The landing page's only data call. Until 2026-08-29 it ran the full check suite
inline (CoreChecksRunner.run_all_checks), including a DAG traversal per expired-
with-stock raw material -- ~285 queries / ~660ms on whistlebird_test (48 expired).
It now reads the expired_materials slice from the shared per-org system-findings
cache (see /api/core/system-findings override) and runs only the cheap checks
live. WARM path: 1 SELECT for the cached row. COLD path (empty cache, once per NZ
day per org or after a mutation): +~4 bookkeeping statements (fetch, advisory
lock, re-fetch, upsert) around the same compute.
The E2E fixture org has ONE expired raw material, so its DAG is trivial and this
route's fixture query count barely moved (38 -> 39 on a cold miss). The point of
the change is that the count NO LONGER SCALES with expired-material history --
measured warm on whistlebird_test: ~660ms -> ~100ms. queries.budget carries
headroom for the cold-miss bookkeeping; ceiling stays where only an N+1 lands.
Added 2026-08-27 with the endpoint (docs/core-load-performance-design.md). This is
the single call /core makes on first paint, replacing a four-call fan-out plus a
duplicate processes?include_steps=true. Its whole value is a query count that does
NOT scale with an org's history: a fixed set of SQL aggregates + one bounded
(<=20) active-execution fetch + one bounded (<=6) gap fetch. The tight queries
ceiling exists to catch an N+1 creeping back onto this path -- e.g. per-active-
execution process-name lookups if the joinedload is dropped.
PLACEHOLDER pending a measured run on the E2E fixture org: recalibrate budget to
the observed median and pin queries at the observed value per SKILL.md.
